epic.title: EPIC-054: Add Google AI Overviews as a Tracked Surface
epic.functionalNeed:
Google AI Overviews is the AI summary shown at the top of Google Search results. For many audiences it is the AI answer they see most, and today GEO cannot say whether a brand appears in it: it has no official API, so the analysis does not track it.

The goal is to add AI Overviews as one more engine of the analysis, with the same metrics, the same question panel and the same exports as the other engines. The answer can only be read on the rendered Google page, so this epic uses the rendered capture and the shared answer reader of GEO-678 (Natural Answer Collection and Parsing), and the full answer card of GEO-1498 (Natural Answer Display). It adds what is specific to AI Overviews: Google does not show an AI Overview for every query, there is no API to fall back on, and the answer can carry images.

Production capture waits for the vendor contract (GEO-678) and the approval to capture the Google surfaces. The legal sign-off on UI capture is obtained (11 Nov 2026). (Updated 2026-11-12) Google AI Mode is a different surface, in GEO-1006.

Change log: 12 Nov 2026, after the review of the stories GEO-1595 to GEO-1600: a new organisation needs at least one engine (story 1.1), a run with no applicable engine fails (story 1.2), softer "Not triggered" tab text (story 1.3), full engine order (story 1.6), legal sign-off status and vendor spend (scope boundaries).

The architect will go into the implementation details.

---

Naming

| Where | Text |
|---|---|
| Engine name, everywhere an engine name shows (wizard, Manage Scope, back office, filters, pills, tabs, exports) | "Google AI Overviews" |
| Compact pills (4 engines or more), as today | Logo only, "Google AI Overviews" in the tooltip |
| Stored description, not shown, as for every engine today (en-GB, en-US) | "An AI-generated summary from Google, powered by Gemini, shown above Google Search results with links to its sources." |
| Stored description (fr-FR) | "Un résumé généré par l'IA de Google, propulsé par Gemini, affiché au-dessus des résultats de recherche Google avec des liens vers ses sources." |
| Stored description (es-ES) | "Un resumen generado por la IA de Google, impulsado por Gemini, que aparece encima de los resultados de búsqueda de Google con enlaces a sus fuentes." |

Logo: the Google "G" in its four colours, next to the name "AI Overviews". The file is attached to this epic (google-g.svg) and is also in the Onclusive Design System brand logos. Google gives AI Overviews no icon of its own, and the Gemini spark is already the logo of the Gemini engine in GEO: the spark would make the two engines look the same. On the wizard and Manage Scope card, the border colour is Google green (#34A853), and the same colour is the engine colour in the Brand Territory pie: Gemini is already blue, so a third blue would make the engines look the same.
scope: GEO-1595 STORY-54.1: Select AI Overviews as an engine
GEO-1596 STORY-54.2: Capture the AI Overview per country
GEO-1597 STORY-54.3: Handle the prompts where Google shows no AI Overview
GEO-1598 STORY-54.4: Read the AI Overview like any other answer
GEO-1599 STORY-54.5: Read the AI Overview in the question panel
GEO-1600 STORY-54.6: Show AI Overviews everywhere engines show

scopeBoundaries.Dependencies:
- GEO-678: the rendered capture, the vendor layer, the country setting and the shared reader. Without them stories 1.2 and 1.4 cannot ship.
- GEO-1498: the full answer card and the "Not counted" state. The images and the fullscreen viewer of story 1.5 are moved from GEO-1498 to this epic and to GEO-1006, and are built once, in whichever of the two ships first.
scopeBoundaries.Vendor spend: - Each AI Overviews capture costs 7 Cloro credits, whether Google shows an AI Overview or not. No daily budget and no credit alert are built: the team watches the Cloro vendor dashboard (Updated 2026-11-12)

outOfScope: The queries Google runs behind the AI Overview, and the AI Overview of a follow-up search.
The vendor contract (GEO-678). The legal sign-off on UI capture is obtained (11 Nov 2026).
Approval to capture the Google surfaces: to confirm, the legal sign-off may not cover it.

Before the build, the team measures on a sample of prompts how often Google shows an AI Overview (eg: "AI Overview shown for 12 of 40 questions"), and then we decide whether the analysis shows this share as coverage context.

technicalNotes.heading: What the code adds to the epic text
technicalNotes.text:
- **Back office: creating an organisation now requires at least one engine** (validated by the PM, 2026-11-12, and now an AC of the epic). Today the form shows every engine off, but the backend gives a new organisation every active engine when nothing is ticked (the creation request carries no engine list; the form sends the chosen engines in a second call, only if at least one is ticked). Left as is, AI Overviews would be granted to every new organisation created without ticking anything, which contradicts "off by default". The story sends the engine list in the creation request, makes it required (the Create button is disabled while no engine is ticked, and the API refuses an empty list), stores it in the same transaction as the organisation, and removes the implicit "every active engine" default. Editing an organisation is unchanged. Existing organisations already do not have the engine and are not changed (no backfill).
- "After Gemini" needs the order of the later engines to be shifted: the current orders are 1 to 5 with no gap. The shift is relative, because the production values were not checked. The order everywhere is the database one (validated by the PM, 2026-11-12, and written in story 1.6 of the epic): ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Overviews, the free slot kept for Google AI Mode, then Grok, Claude, Perplexity. In the PowerPoint export the engines read Grok then Claude (accepted by the PM).
- Engine presentation (names, logos, colours, order) is hard-coded in about eleven places and nothing tests it. The story starts with a separate refactor, with zero change for the five existing engines and characterization tests written first, then adds the engine.
- The engine row is created inactive and activated per environment: the epic says production capture waits for the legal sign-off, the vendor contract and the approval to capture the Google surfaces, and the engine has no API to fall back on.

technicalNotes.heading: Scope note
technicalNotes.text: Two PRs, both to the integration branch: PR 1 "engine presentation refactor" (no behaviour change), PR 2 "AI Overviews engine" (one database migration, creation of an organisation with its engines, back office, wizard, Manage Scope). First story of the epic: the others depend on its migration. Design: GEO-1017 (Figma "Measure - GEO Module"), logo `google-g.svg` attached to GEO-1005, border and pie colour #34A853.

technicalNotes.heading: What the code and the vendor measurements add to the epic text
technicalNotes.text:
- The vendor has no AI Overviews route: the AI Overview is part of a Google Search capture (another endpoint, request body and response root than ChatGPT and Gemini), so the capture layer becomes a registry of per-surface strategies keyed by data.
- "No API fallback" cannot be a single flag. Today every failed capture goes back to the engine's API, the organisation guards also downgrade to the API, and a report only completes if the capture step itself emits a terminal event. The story makes "no API request, ever, for this engine" an invariant in the backend, the message and Flink, and writes the exemption of the epic 50 rule ("every failed capture falls back to the API") in the docs.
- An excluded country is not refused by the vendor: it answers like "Google showed no AI Overview", billed. So the backend sends no question at all for an excluded country, in both analysis phases, with consistent totals.
- "Show more": the vendor does not document it, but all 31 recorded vendor AI Overviews end like a complete answer (closing questions or a closing sentence, none stops mid-list), which indicates the vendor returns the unfolded text. It is indirect evidence (the content changes on each call), so the story carries a verification task on more queries.
- Capture failure rate on real prompts (PM request, 2026-11-12): 0 failed captures out of 165 (three analyses; fr-FR, es-ES, ar-MA, en-GB, en-US; HTTP 200 on every call, median 10.7 s, maximum 28.2 s). Small sample, one call per prompt and pass.

technicalNotes.heading: Questions for the PM
technicalNotes.text:
**P1 — A run where every question is skipped.** The epic keeps creation allowed when AI Overviews is the only engine and every selected country is excluded, and does not say what the run then does. At run time there is nothing to dispatch.

- Option A — the run fails with a clear message ("no selected engine applies to the selected countries"), like an analysis with no usable engine today. Option B — the run completes with zero responses and shows nothing.
- Answered by the PM on 2026-11-12: option A, the run fails with the message "No selected engine applies to the selected countries."
- If unanswered: A ships. Without any rule the code would leave the report in "processing" and announce "Analysis complete" with an empty status, which must not ship.

technicalNotes.heading: Scope note
technicalNotes.text: Depends on STORY-54.1 (the engine row and its columns). Covers the capture strategies, the no-API invariant, the excluded-country table and its use in both analysis phases, and the amber lines in the Review step, the add-country dialog and Manage Scope. Deploy order: Flink first, backend second. Out of repository: the engine key to add to the Flink provider list in the deployment overlays. Production capture also waits for the vendor contract and the approval to capture the Google surfaces (decisions of GEO-678).

technicalNotes.heading: What the code and the vendor measurements add to the epic text
technicalNotes.text:
- "Not triggered" is an observed fact and is stored as a result: a new reason on the existing "not counted" mechanism. "Not available" is a configuration fact (no question is dispatched for an excluded country, see STORY-54.2) and is computed when the panel is read: the question detail only loads successful rows, so the backend has to build the entry of an engine that has no row.
- A failed capture is not a reason: stories 50.6 and 50.9 settled that it stays a failed row with its cause. It shows in the panel as for every engine today ("No data available", the panel loads only successful rows); the failure is recorded and visible in the report health view.
- Without a distinct success path, an absent AI Overview would end as a cut capture and, with no API, as a failed row. The vendor answers "200" with the AI Overview key absent, billed.
- Measured: 24 of 25 test queries had an AI Overview. The one absence was absent in 5 of 5 vendor calls while a signed-in browser showed one, so "not triggered" describes what the vendor's session received. The epic's wording is kept as written.
- Share of prompts with an AI Overview on real prompts (PM request, 2026-11-12): 97 % over 165 prompts of three analyses (160 with, 5 without on the first pass; 159 and 6 on the second). By market: en-US 100 % (15), es-ES 100 % (30), ar-MA 100 % (30), fr-FR 98 % (60), en-GB 87 % (30). The absences concentrate on generic visibility prompts: four UK visibility prompts had none on both passes, the other absences differ from one pass to the other, so "not triggered" is not stable for every prompt. Small sample, UK from a single analysis.
- The new reason needs its database CHECK replaced before any writer is deployed; a build older than the value fails when it loads such a row.

technicalNotes.heading: Scope note
technicalNotes.text: Depends on STORY-54.2. Design: GEO-1017, frame 04d "Not counted". Includes one database migration (the "not counted" reason CHECK), to be applied before the backend that writes the new reason is deployed.

technicalNotes.heading: What the code and the vendor measurements add to the epic text
technicalNotes.text:
- The shared reader needs no change and has no engine-specific branch. It reads one grouped call per question across all engines, so an extra engine adds records to each call (checked with six).
- The place of each citation is the real work. A captured answer carries no citation place today (plain text, vendor citation pills without offsets). The vendor gives the places only in an optional markdown version of the answer, and story 50.9 (AC4) says parsing must never rely on markdown created by a capture vendor. The story keeps that rule and delivers the epic's criterion: the capture step reads the markdown once and stores plain text plus the places; the reader never parses vendor markdown.
- The captured path also has no way to receive citation places and no guard that the places match the stored text: the story adds both.
- Page residue: none was found in 24 measured AI Overviews, so the cleaning is minimal and defensive (whole-line removals only). The engine's own closing questions are prose and are kept.
- Images, videos, shopping cards, organic results and ads stay in the raw capture and are never read or counted.

technicalNotes.text: Depends on STORY-54.2 (the capture strategy and its request) and STORY-54.3 (blank answers are excluded before the reader). No database migration. No frontend change expected (checked in STORY-54.5).

technicalNotes.heading: Deviation from the epic text
technicalNotes.text:
The criteria about images (the second to the fifth, and the sixth and seventh for what they say about images) cannot be met from the data the capture vendor returns, so this story builds nothing for them.

- Covered by this story, as verification and tests with no change expected: the first criterion (the full answer card) and the last (no numbered citation).
- Already true because images are never rendered: the sixth (an image that does not load is hidden) and the seventh (images are not counted in the header).
- Not covered: the second to the fifth (images in the answer, captions and credit, the fullscreen viewer). They stay visibly unmet; question P1 is settled (option A, 2026-11-12) and they move to GEO-1608.

Why: the vendor returns **no image inside the AI Overview**: 0 images in 24 measured AI Overviews. What it returns: "videos" (title, source, platform, duration, a thumbnail hosted by Google) in 19 of 24, and, in 1 of 24, a block of page-level images (title, source, link, thumbnail) that Google shows on the results page, with no position in the answer. The epic's own example (the "Big Three" carriers image) is not reproducible: the matching measured query returned none. The application also has no image viewer today and its answer renderer ignores images on purpose. The viewer the epic says is "built once, in whichever epic ships first" is not built here; epic 55 inherits the same question. The measured sample is small (24 AI Overviews, US and FR, queries written for the test): a wider sample before closing question P1 is cheap.

technicalNotes.heading: Questions for the PM
technicalNotes.text:
**P1 — Images in the AI Overview.** The epic asks for images shown in the answer at the place Google showed them, with caption, credit and a fullscreen view. The capture vendor returns no image inside the AI Overview (see above).

- Option A — postpone images (nothing is built; the criteria stay visibly unmet) and revisit when the vendor or the design changes.
- Option B — show the AI Overview's videos in a block apart, below the answer (not "at the place Google showed them").
- Option C — show the page-level images in a block apart, when present (1 in 24).
- Answered on 2026-11-12 (PM proposal, team agreed): option A for this story. Images of the answer card (all engines, ChatGPT first, frames 08a and 08b) move to the follow-up story GEO-1608 (STORY-53.10) under GEO-1498.
- If unanswered: A ships. Users see the AI Overview text and sources but no image or video, which is also what the vendor's data supports.
- Note for B and C: the thumbnails are Google-hosted URLs (or inline base64 data), so showing them loads images from another site, and the application sets no image content-security rule today. That would be a hosting and security decision to take then; it does not arise while A holds.

technicalNotes.heading: Scope note
technicalNotes.text: Frontend verification and tests only; no migration, no backend change expected. Depends on STORY-54.3 and STORY-54.4. Design: GEO-1017 frames 01, 02, 03, 05 (answer card). Frames 08a and 08b are cited by the epic but have no recorded node id in the repository: the story asks to locate them for the day images are decided.
